title: Adding numerators and keeping one denominator
statement: To add fractions you add the numerators and keep the denominator, whichever denominator is written, because the denominator is just a label that does not take part in the sum.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: add two fractions with unlike denominators
evidence_patterns.signature: response numerator = a + c; response denominator is one of the given denominators (usually the first or the larger), with no conversion of the addends
evidence_patterns.notes: Like-denominator items are answered correctly, which is the discriminator against math.frac.add-across.

discriminators.vs_slip: Consistent across unlike-denominator items; the learner can state the rule ("the bottom stays") when asked.

vs.math.frac.add-across: Give a like-denominator item. This belief answers 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4 correctly; add-across gives 3/8.

conflicts_with.label: CCSS 5.NF.A.1: add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators

resolved_by.label: CCSS 5.NF.A.1: add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators
